1# Detection maps and coincidence summing
2
3The source is `docs/paper/APS_Coincidence_Algebra-14.pdf`, Section II.B,
4Eqs. (28)-(33). Eq. (32) is the target probability vector. The implementation uses
5an isotropic array of N identical detectors. Efficiencies are probabilities
6for the whole array, conditional on gamma emission; they are not per-detector
7efficiencies. Supply measured or simulated values for your setup, keyed by
8transition name. No total-efficiency curve is built in.
9
10For physical total transition coefficient t and gamma fraction q=1/(1+alpha):
11
12    h = t q peak_efficiency
13    a = t q total_efficiency / N
14    o = t (1 - q total_efficiency / N)
15
16`DetectionMaps::FullEnergyHit`, `TotalHit`, and `SummingOut` implement these
17three edge maps. The total efficiency includes both full-energy absorption
18and partial deposition, including Compton scattering. Thus a photon can sum
19an observed peak out even when its own peak efficiency is zero.
20
21Conversion belongs inside the complement in o. Multiplying the entire
22no-hit probability by q would discard converted transitions that still feed
23the next level. These maps model gamma interactions; conversion electrons,
24atomic relaxation, inter-detector scattering correlations, angular correlations,
25and timing windows require additional detector-response modelling.
26
27All maps preserve stationary coefficients. Longer paths receive the product
28of their edge factors. They do not renormalize mapped vectors. Apply the maps
29to IC-inclusive physical coefficients, not to an already emission-weighted
30vector, to avoid counting conversion twice.
31
32## Usage
33
34```cpp
35#include "COINAlgebra/Detection/DetectionMaps.h"
36
37// peakEfficiencies and totalEfficiencies: maps supplied for your array.
38// alpha: coefficient map returned by BuildGammaQuiver.
39DetectionMaps maps(peakEfficiencies, totalEfficiencies, detectorCount, alpha);
40auto branch = projectors.BranchingProjector(decay);
41auto transition = decay - branch;
42auto hit = maps.FullEnergyHit(transition);
43auto avoid = maps.SummingOut(transition);
44auto summedPaths = maps.SummingInExpansion(algebra, transition);
45
46auto corrected = pb.SummingFeedingVector(decay, maps);
47double peakProbability = algebra.PathForm(corrected, DecayVector(observedPath));
48```
49
50Omitting alpha (or passing an empty map) explicitly assumes no conversion.
51A nonempty alpha map must contain each used edge. Required efficiency entries
52must exist; all efficiencies must be finite and satisfy 0 <= peak <= total
53<= 1, alpha must be finite and nonnegative, and N must be positive.
54
55`tests/integration/test_133Ba_gamma_quiver.C` defines the detector setup inside
56its no-argument macro: `totalEfficiency = 0.7` for every transition and
57`detectorCount = 64. Edit these constants for your setup. Each run prints the
58emission/detection tables followed by connected summing contributions and
59endpoint-combined corrected peaks. The uniform 0.7 is an illustrative input,
60not a measured efficiency curve.
61The macro retains its existing illustrative peak-efficiency values; replace
62those too when changing the detector setup.
63
64## Connected summing
65
66`SummingInExpansion` constructs only positive powers:
67
68    H = h + h^2/N + h^3/N^2 + ... .
69
70It accepts single-edge terms, and leaves each connected path as a distinct
71basis term. An isolated gamma's efficiency is not divided by N: the first hit
72can occur anywhere in the array; each additional summed hit must be in that
73same detector. The code currently uses N^(k-1) under this whole-array
74efficiency convention. Eq. (31) as printed instead has N^(k+1); this is an
75author-confirmed typo; the agreed correction is recorded as
76[PA-001](../paper/ERRATA.md#pa-001--detector-count-exponent).
77No stationary term belongs in H, the central factor after identity subtraction
78in Eq. (32).
79
80With O=1+o+o^2+... and E the sum of stationary paths at terminal levels:
81
82    Gamma_path = V_target(b O) H V_source(O E).
83
84This follows the intent of Eq. (32) with a terminal restriction on the lower
85factor. The unrestricted V_source(O) printed there counts every partial
86suffix as well as the completed cascade. For example, an observed upper
87transition followed by a lower transition would acquire 1+o_lower instead of
88o_lower. Restricting to terminal endpoints prevents that overcounting; this is
89an explicit boundary-condition adjustment to the printed Eq. (32), still
90awaiting review in [PA-002](../paper/ERRATA.md#pa-002--lower-propagation-boundary).
91Terminal levels are quiver sinks, including multiple sinks.
92The observation window is assumed to include the full cascade to these sinks.
93
94`SummingFeedingVector` implements this formula. The resulting vector retains
95individual path contributions. `PathForm` collects paths with equal source
96and target, giving the direct peak plus connected cascades with the same
97energy difference. Sum-only paths exist even where no direct edge is present.
98This does not model finite energy resolution or group unrelated paths that
99happen to have equal gamma-energy sums.
100
101## Scope
102
103These calculations use only the path algebra. Observed photons must form a
104connected path; sums of non-connected transitions and gated spectra are outside
105this implementation.
106
107`SummingFeedingVector` requires an acyclic quiver, nonnegative finite initial
108populations, single-edge transition terms, and total outgoing coefficients
109summing to one at every nonterminal level. It uses the decay-vector
110coefficients rather than stored transition probabilities. It enumerates
111higher-order contributions, so output size can grow rapidly with cascade size.
112

118nonempty subsets of observed photons, comparing connected-path results on a branching scheme with two initial populations
119and two terminal levels.
